entities.summary: The Iowa class was a class of six fast battleships ordered by the United States Navy in 1939 and 1940. They were initially intended to intercept fast capital ships such as the Japanese Kongō-class battlecruisers and serve as the "fast wing" of the U.S. battle line. The Iowa class was designed to meet the Second London Naval Treaty's "escalator clause" limit of 45,000-long-ton (45,700 t) standard displacement. Beginning in August 1942, four vessels, Iowa, New Jersey, Missouri, and Wisconsin, were completed; two more, Illinois and Kentucky, were laid down but canceled in 1945 and 1958, respectively, before completion, and both hulls were scrapped in 1958–1959.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Iowa class battleships played a crucial role in World War II, serving as part of the U.S. Pacific Fleet and participating in key battles such as the Battle of Midway. Their design influenced subsequent capital ship classes, including the T45-class guided-missile cruisers.
